excerpt: Send Traces and APM Data
Follow a single request across all microservices with a flamegraph view that shows every span, its duration, and parent-child relationships.
Search and filter traces by service, operation, duration, or any span attribute.
Visualize dependencies between services, databases, and messaging systems, and spot which endpoint is receiving failed calls, sized by incoming call rate.
Analyze how requests flow through a sequence of services or spans and identify drop-off points.
Collect logs from files, stdout, FluentBit/FluentD/Logstash, OpenTelemetry SDKs, HTTP endpoints, and cloud services.
Search, filter, and analyze logs with List, Time Series, and Table views. Stream live logs in real time.
Parse, transform, and enrich logs before storage using SigNoz's functional pipeline builder.
Set up alerts on log patterns, counts, or attribute values.
Collect metrics from applications, infrastructure, and existing Prometheus setups. SigNoz also derives APM metrics from traces automatically.
Use the Metrics Explorer to query and visualize data with a visual builder or advanced query languages like PromQL and ClickHouse SQL.
Build panels in a dedicated editor: seven panel types with a live preview, switchable mid-edit without losing your formatting, units or thresholds.
Filter everything with variables: dynamic, query, custom and textbox variables.
Drill down from any panel: jump into the underlying logs and traces, break out by an attribute, create an alert seeded from the panel, or download it as PNG, SVG or CSV.
Publish a dashboard publicly: a separate flow that generates a public URL anyone can open without logging in.
Manage dashboards as code
Edit a dashboard as JSON: read, copy, download or hand-edit the whole spec in the app, without going through the API.
Complete guide to migrating from Datadog to SigNoz. How to migrate metrics, traces/APM, logs, dashboards, and alerts.
The process can be done incrementally—you can migrate one signal type at a time while running both platforms in parallel.
Bridge Solution: Datadog Receiver
Roles are the core unit of access control in SigNoz. A role groups transactions together — when a principal is assigned a role, they receive all the transactions that role contains.
Service accounts provide a secure way to grant programmatic API access to SigNoz without tying credentials to individual users. Use them for CI/CD pipelines, automation scripts, external integrations
Your application emits gen_ai.* spans and metrics through standard OpenTelemetry libraries, exports them over OTLP, and SigNoz stores and queries them next to the rest of your application telemetry.
